title: Start a conversation
content: Use hello or hi in casual situations. Use good morning before noon and good evening later in the day. To introduce yourself, say: My name is ___. Ask another person: What is your name?
exercise: Complete the introduction: My name ___ Ana.

title: Subject pronouns
summary: Choose who performs the action in a sentence.
content: English subject pronouns include I, you, he, she, it, we, and they. A subject pronoun usually appears before the verb: She reads. They study.
exercise: Choose the pronoun: ___ are learning English. (we / us)

title: The verb be
summary: Use am, is, and are to describe people and things.
content: Use am with I, is with he, she, or it, and are with you, we, or they. Examples: I am ready. She is a student. We are here.

title: A, an, and the
content: Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound: a book, an apple. Use the when the listener knows which specific thing you mean: the book on the table.

title: Present simple
summary: Talk about habits and facts in the present.
content: Use the base verb with I, you, we, and they. Add -s or -es with he, she, and it: I work; she works. Use do or does to make most questions.

title: Past simple
summary: Describe finished actions in the past.
content: Regular verbs often add -ed: walk becomes walked. Some verbs are irregular: go becomes went. Use did plus the base verb in questions and negatives.
exercise: Complete: Yesterday, we ___ to the park. (go)

title: Build a clear sentence
summary: Arrange words in a natural English sentence.
content: A common English sentence order is subject, verb, object: The learner reads a book. Adjectives usually come before the noun: a useful lesson.
exercise: Put these in order: (English / speak / I)

title: Ask useful questions
summary: Use what, where, when, who, why, and how.
content: Question words ask for different information: what for a thing, where for a place, when for a time, who for a person, why for a reason, and how for a method or condition.
exercise: Ask about a place: ___ do you live? (Where / When)

title: Everyday vocabulary
summary: Build useful words for daily routines.
content: Useful routine verbs include wake up, eat, work, study, travel, relax, and sleep. Put them into short sentences to remember their meanings in context.
exercise: Choose the routine verb: At night, I ___. (sleep / travel)

title: Make a polite request
summary: Ask for help in a friendly, respectful way.
content: Could you help me, please? and Would you mind repeating that? are polite ways to ask for help. Please softens a request; thank you acknowledges help.
exercise: Complete a polite request: Could you ___ me, please? (help / helps)

title: Describe with adjectives
summary: Add details about people, places, and things.
content: Adjectives describe nouns: a quiet room, a helpful tutor, a difficult question. In English they usually appear before the noun or after a linking verb: The room is quiet.
exercise: Choose the adjective: The lesson is ___. (useful / usefully)
